record.original_question: Assume the object is a sparse crystallographic model consisting of a background term plus finitely many weighted Dirac masses at unknown positions in the plane, and let a Schwartz-class probe be given. From phaseless ptychographic measurements of the form A(f)(r, xi) = |F(f · S_r w)(xi)|^2 over probe shifts r and frequencies xi in a measurement domain Omega, can one recover all atom positions t_j and complex weights a_j?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4. Suppose the signal f is given by the model (7) and let w P S(R2) be the probe. Given the measurements of the form A(f)(r, ξ) = |F(f · Srw)(ξ)|2, ξ P Ω, r P R, recover the atom positions tj and weights aj for j P {1, . . . , N}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $w \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ be a fixed Schwartz-class probe function, and for $r \in \mathbb{R}^2$ let $S_r w$ denote the shifted probe defined by $(S_r w)(x) = w(x-r)$. Consider an unknown signal of "sparse crystallographic" type
$$ f(x) = b(x) + \sum_{j=1}^{N} a_j\, \delta_{t_j}(x), $$
where $b$ is a known (or otherwise specified) background term, $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the positions $t_1,\dots,t_N \in \mathbb{R}^2$ are pairwise distinct and unknown, and the weights $a_1,\dots,a_N \in \mathbb{C}$ are unknown. For a measurement domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and a set of admissible probe shifts $R \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, suppose one is given the phaseless ptychographic measurements
$$ A(f)(r,\xi) = \bigl|\mathcal{F}\bigl(f \cdot S_r w\bigr)(\xi)\bigr|^2, \qquad r \in R,\ \xi \in \Omega, $$
where $\mathcal{F}$ denotes the Fourier transform on $\mathbb{R}^2$. 

Determine whether the data $\{A(f)(r,\xi) : r \in R,\ \xi \in \Omega\}$ uniquely determine all atom positions $t_j$ and complex weights $a_j$ ($j=1,\dots,N$), and identify sufficient conditions on $w$, $R$, $\Omega$, and the configuration $\{t_j\}$ under which exact recovery is possible (together with a constructive recovery procedure).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2025 survey of phase retrieval problems. While related super-resolution phase retrieval results exist for sparse signals (e.g., Prony-based methods), no general uniqueness/recovery guarantees for the sparse crystallographic ptychographic model with Schwartz probes appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: Phasebook: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems in phase retrieval, including sparse crystallographic ptychography recovery.
status_evidence.claim: The recovery problem is presented as an unresolved open question.

status_evidence.title: Prony-Based Super-Resolution Phase Retrieval of Sparse, Multidimensional Signals
status_evidence.snippet: Prony-based super-resolution phase retrieval methods for sparse signals.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial results exist for super-resolution phase retrieval of sparse signals but do not directly resolve the ptychographic crystallographic case.
